cf_resolve.record: timestamp size at +0x00, CF id (dword) at +0x08, Status code at +0x10, subcode bytes at +0x11..+0x15, message pointer at +0x18
rules: cf id comes from 0x5d8d4b0(cf_obj), stored at record+0x08 (0 for the default column family)
cf_obj null: timestamp size is taken from batch+0x38 and the code is 0
otherwise virtual slot 0x28 is called on cf_obj; its result P null means timestamp size 0 and code 0; P non-null means timestamp size *(P+0x28)
CF id 0 (default CF) with a timestamp size differing from *(batch+0x38) carries InvalidArgument 'Default cf timestamp size mismatch'
a nonzero code in the record is propagated into the middle's out Status

guard.note: mapped in full in PR #3202; guard_main.txt is re-shipped byte-identical from that packet

cf_timestamp.text: Cannot call this method on column family enabling timestamp

entity_too_large.text: wide column entity is too large

merge_operator.text: Provide a merge_operator when opening DB

no_cf_handle.text: Cannot call this method without a column family handle

merge.second_gate: after the timestamp guard the wrapper calls virtual slot 0x30 on the rcx-object and checks *(result+0x5c8); null returns NotSupported 'Provide a merge_operator when opening DB'

putentity.size_limits: key length > 0xFFFFFFFF returns InvalidArgument 'key is too large'; entity size (computed by 0x5fb4f60) > 0xFFFFFFFF returns InvalidArgument 'wide column entity is too large'

pipeline.dispatch: on a middle success the implementation calls virtual slot 0xe0 on the rsi-object with (out, rsi-object, rdx, batch); the callee identity is not resolved from the file
pipeline.impl: constructs a WriteBatch on the stack via 0x5fb9f90, calls its middle callee with (temp Status, batch, op args); on a middle failure the Status is moved into out (PutEntity deep-copies the message via 0x61cf610 because its shared cleanup frees the temp message); the batch is destroyed with 0x5fb7ee0 on every path
pipeline.inner: appends one record to rep_ (type byte, varint32 CF id when nonzero, varint32 key length + key bytes + ts_size NUL bytes, varint32 value length + value for Put/Merge/PutEntity, end key instead of a value for DeleteRange), sets its flag bit, bumps the rep_ count by one, runs the shared hash-combine epilogue (0x61c3c00/0x61c3530)
pipeline.middle: fills the 0x28-byte CF resolution record via 0x5fbbc90; a nonzero code is propagated into out; timestamp size 0 takes the tail callee (plain key); timestamp size nonzero builds a zero-filled string of that size and calls the inner appender (key + timestamp); PutEntity has no tail: timestamp size nonzero returns InvalidArgument, and a null column-family handle returns InvalidArgument
pipeline.record: [type byte][varint32 CF id, only when cf_id != 0][varint32 key length][key bytes + ts_size NUL bytes][varint32 value length][value bytes] (Put, Merge, PutEntity only; DeleteRange carries an end key instead of a value)
pipeline.tail: the timestamp-size-zero path; writes the same record-type byte as its inner with the plain key (Put 0x01/0x05, Delete 0x00/0x04, SingleDelete 0x07/0x08, DeleteRange 0x0f/0x0e, Merge by push_back); its length-encoding, count bump and hash epilogue are not resolved this cycle
pipeline.wrapper: calls the timestamp guard 0x5d58810 with (stack-temp Status, factory, object); a guard failure copies the Status into out (message deep-copied with 0x61cf610) and returns; on success all arguments are forwarded to the implementation

status.layout: code u16 at +0x00, subcode u32 at +0x02, message pointer at +0x08

unknowns: what the virtual slot 0xe0 dispatch does with the batch (a DB::Write is the natural reading, not a pinned fact)
the exact object identities behind the wrapper/impl argument slots
the full internals of the five tail callees (length-encoding, count bump, hash epilogue)
the entity-size computation behind 0x5fb4f60 (the model uses key length + value length as its documented approximation; the 0xFFFFFFFF threshold is pinned)
the batch post-append hash-combine epilogue (0x61c3c00/0x61c3530 with magic constants)
when the middle's timestamp error can fire given the wrapper guard already checks a timestamp indicator on a different object (rcx vs rdx)
